Earlier clicks (59,4) and (14,49) didn't move the token… but wait, those were when the token was at (59,4) — clicking on the token itself did nothing, and clicking on the ball did nothing either. So the rule might be: click a trail dot to move the token one step in the direction of that dot? Or click the next dot to move there.
Let me test: click the next dot at (49,14) and see if the token moves to (49,14). If so, I can just repeatedly click dots ahead to move the token along the trail all the way to the ball.
Dots ahead: (49,14), (47,16), (45,18), (43,20), (41,22), (39,24), (37,26), (35,28), (33,30), (31,32), (29,34), (27,36), (25,38), (23,40), (21,42), (19,44), (17,46). Then the ball is at (11-17, 46-52), with center around (14,49).
16 more dot clicks to reach (17,46), then probably one more to reach the ball. Each click consumes 2 timer pixels. Timer is currently 60 pixels → 30 actions available. 16-17 clicks should be fine.
But wait — should I click each dot, or does clicking a far dot move the token multiple steps? Let me test with (49,14) first. Actually, to save actions, let me test with a farther dot, say (45,18): if the token jumps to (45,18), then clicks teleport to the clicked dot. If it only moves to (49,14), then it's one step at a time.
